Linux Mint Cinnamon.label: The easy all-rounder
Linux Mint Cinnamon.description: Familiar controls, proven tools, and little day-to-day maintenance. Cinnamon offers a traditional desktop.

Linux Mint Xfce.label: Lightweight and practical
Linux Mint Xfce.description: The more resource-friendly Mint edition: a classic desktop, easy to use, and suitable for older computers.

Zorin OS Core.label: An elegant transition
Zorin OS Core.description: A beginner-friendly Ubuntu derivative with a polished, familiar interface and an emphasis on switching easily.

Ubuntu GNOME.label: The popular all-rounder
Ubuntu GNOME.description: Widely used, well documented, and supported by a large software ecosystem. GNOME offers a distinct, streamlined workflow.

Kubuntu.label: Ubuntu with KDE flexibility
Kubuntu.description: An Ubuntu foundation with Plasma: familiar desktop interaction and extensive settings out of the box.

Debian GNOME.label: The steady classic
Debian GNOME.description: Conservative package maintenance and a solid foundation for people who value consistency over the newest releases.

Debian KDE.label: Stability meets flexibility
Debian KDE.description: Debian’s steady foundation paired with the versatile Plasma desktop: conservative at its core, customizable on the surface.

Fedora Workstation.label: Modern Linux with GNOME
Fedora Workstation.description: Up-to-date technologies, a focused GNOME desktop, and a relatively fast release cycle.

Fedora KDE.label: Current and customizable
Fedora KDE.description: Fedora with KDE Plasma: modern software and an interface you can personalize without much manual work.

openSUSE Leap KDE.label: A measured KDE foundation
openSUSE Leap KDE.description: Focused on consistency, with KDE Plasma, management tools, and Btrfs snapshots for rollbacks when configured appropriately.

openSUSE Tumbleweed KDE.label: Rolling release with a safety net
openSUSE Tumbleweed KDE.description: Very recent packages, KDE Plasma, and well-integrated Btrfs/Snapper rollback support in a typical installation.

MX Linux Xfce.label: Practical and resource-friendly
MX Linux Xfce.description: A Debian-based distribution with a lightweight Xfce desktop and its own setup and management utilities.

Linux Lite.label: Simple on older PCs
Linux Lite.description: A lightweight Ubuntu-based desktop distribution with familiar controls and an emphasis on an easy start.

elementary OS.label: Consistent by design
elementary OS.description: A carefully designed minimalist desktop with its own interface and intentionally limited customization.

Pop!_OS COSMIC.label: Productivity with COSMIC
Pop!_OS COSMIC.description: An independent, modern COSMIC desktop with thoughtful window workflows and many built-in options.

Bazzite KDE.label: Gaming first, maintenance second
Bazzite KDE.description: A gaming-focused, image-based Fedora system with Steam integration, KDE, and straightforward system rollback.

Nobara KDE.label: Fedora tuned for gamers
Nobara KDE.description: A Fedora derivative customized for gaming and multimedia, maintained as a more specialized community project.

CachyOS KDE.label: Performance for enthusiasts
CachyOS KDE.description: An Arch-based distribution with performance tuning and fresh packages, aimed at people who enjoy actively managing their system.

EndeavourOS KDE.label: Arch with a head start
EndeavourOS KDE.description: Close to Arch Linux, but easier to get started with. Rolling releases and ongoing maintenance remain part of the experience.

Arch Linux (Eigenbau).label: Build your own Linux
Arch Linux (Eigenbau).description: A minimal starting point with maximum control. Installation, desktop selection, and maintenance are largely up to you.

NixOS KDE.label: Your system as configuration
NixOS KDE.description: Declarative system configuration and reproducible setups with powerful rollback concepts, but a substantial learning curve.

Omarchy.label: An opinionated tiling workflow
Omarchy.description: A preconfigured Arch/Hyprland environment with keyboard-oriented workflows and deliberate design choices, not a conventional desktop.
